review_description: We had our system installed 3 years ago. At the time we contacted 3 suppliers and Wayne was the only one who came to our house, checked out our different roof angles and suggested a system totally different to the telephone/internet based installers and explained why. Very happy with their service and installation.I'm writing this review 3 years later because recently our Goodwee inverter had a melt down. We made a phone call to Solar Dynamics and they arranged one of their technicians to check it out, confirm it needed replacing and arrange the warranty claim with Goodwee. They followed up everything. We did not have to do anything other than wait for Goodwee to supply the new inverter. As soon as it was delivered to Solar Dynamics they installed it at our house and made sure it was connected to my phone app. The new inverter is running superbly.We were lucky to have purchased an inverter that the manufacturer honored the warranty. But more importantly we had the full back up and support of our installer. Well done Solar Dynamics.

When we decided to add a battery and double our panel capacity, we thought it appropriate to check the market.  SolarQuotes proposed our original supplier, Solar Dynamics, and two other nearby operators,Those two other candidates had an opportunity to demonstrate that they could do better, but they failed badly.  As when we installed the first panels, Wayne at Solar Dynamics was the only candidate to spend time with me, hear what I wanted, and explain the finer details.  Neither of the others listened.  One simply quoted for a Powerwall 2 (yes, a fire hazard for a cedar weatherboard house) and not even the extra panels that were requested.  The other was going to put extra panels in a shaded area.Thanks for keeping the standards up, Wayne and the team at Solar Dynamics.By the way, the Sigen system with 16kWh of storage recommended by Wayne went in with only one slight hitch - it loses the wifi connection.  Solar Dynamics will be installing a wired internet connection in a couple of weeks.  The Sigen is otherwise performing flawlessly and has already carried us safely through a 6 hour blackout that we only knew about because Ausnet sent a message saying they were investigating.  To top that off, we use Amber as our provider and they are already managing the system so that we aren't just saving money - we are making money.No nuclear options needed or considered.

Wayne explained about the basics, cleared my queries (I believe I didn’t ask any foolish questions as I had watched and read about solar technology from the fantastic website of Finn’s solar quotes) and he did a site survey. Suggested the best location for the inverter considering battery installation in future. The installers came and they did a wonderful job and didn’t leave rubbish. The admin staff at solar dynamics did a fantastic job in completing the required paperwork.
First contact with Hermann was great ,gave me all the answers I needed and I used that with the other installers when they rang

The sales and quoting process was straightforward with no over-hyping and useful advice was given on optimum design and layout of panels for our site.Installation went ahead earlier than scheduled, which was a pleasant surprise.Installers were very punctual and super polite and did not mind being asked questions during the install. They were quick and efficient and cleaned up well after the install.

My experience with Solar Dynamics was first rate!  Wayne conducted a thorough site inspection prior to the preparation of his quote and happily answered my subsequent questions in several follow up conversations.  The installation team of three were friendly, professional and thorough. My installation was somewhat challenging, (complex roof presented cabling difficulties, cathedral ceilings etc.), the installers kept me informed of issues when they arose and resolved them in a competent and neat manner, mindful of the installed systems aesthetic appearance as well as its functionality.  The office staff were a delight to deal with and responded to my requests in a prompt and efficient fashion.  The 'icing on the cake' - Solar Dynamics were competitive in their pricing too! I have no hesitation in recommending them to prospective clients.

Right from the initial quote, to on site review, subsequent revised quotes, installation and final electrical inspection, Solar Dynamics were consistently top quality in communication and delivery of the promised product.  The install team were brilliant and hard working on more than warm days on the roof.   Communication from the team in the office was clear and timely.  No question we asked was too silly and treated with respect at all times.  The whole experience was great.
Sales team very helpful before agreeing to quote. Quote sign off very thorough. Installers on time, tidy and polite.Delivered job on time as planned

The up front service was extremely good and a clear solution was provided to meet my desires. The quoting process was also good. Information was provided as to the Govt's help on rebate and interest free loan.The installation was efficient, on time, and looks to be a sensible installation albeit slightly different to that proposed. Quote process was good, I felt like they listened to me instead of trying to sell me the easiest to install system. Came to my house on request before I'd committed to buying to see the install location.After-install support has been great so far.

Sales -quoting process was good - salesman called me and we discussed things right then and there.answered questions on heat-pump and opted to go with oneIn dealing with other sales people -I was told that my area  could not do feed-in AND would be limited to 5 kW for an inverter.  I discussed this with the salesman - Nathan Avins - and he said the no fee-in most likely related to an old transformer taht couldn't be interrogated - or something like that -  I could pay a fee to have a review - in the end I didn't have to pay the fee and we got the review done and WAS ALLOWED TO HAVE FEED-IN.Additionally I had been told that if I ever put a car-charging inverter that this would mean I would have to downgrade my solar inverter as no more than 5 kw of inverter were allowed connected to the grid.  Mr Avis advised that I could go above the 5kw inverter limit with a power meter which would limit the fee-in to 5kW - then any additional inverters would be OK as power to the grid would be throttled to 5kW.I also took your advice and asked them to put a shade cover over the inverter on the west wall  - they did this at cost - as in of the shade cover and no labour cost.The only downside was the install was longer to happen than I would have liked, and they had trouble getting a plumber to do the heat pump install.  But I could not be happier overall - I am now off gas completely with plenty of hot water.   I have recommended solar dynamics to several friends particularly because of Nathan's knowledge to work around some pretty serious obstacles - without which I would have been far less satisfied.Yes they organised all the other stuff - but once again it took longer than advertised - My belief is that is the way things are currently - lots of people off sick and hard to get tradies who are also off sick a lot

Sales and installation team were up front, helpful and encouraged asking questions before and after purchase. Solar Dynamics are a good company to both purchase from and get a sense of what type of system might be appropriate for your needs. Emails/calls were answered within a day and the team handled all the post-installation grid connection paperwork with my electric retailer.At the time of writing, the Q.Cells inverter seems to have an ongoing technical issue where the inverter will periodically give off a "fault" message after sundown. The QCells team have been in regular contact to resolve the issue and have kept me updated on the status of the problem. Our newly commissioned system is 43 x 370W (nominal 15.9kW) Canadian Solar panels, 2xSolarEdge 8250 inverters and a Tesla Powerwall2 with Gateway2 with backup to essential loads (internet, fridges, selected kitchen appliances - not the induction top, office so I can keep working and garage).We went through a few iterations of quoting to finally land on what we thought would be the most suitable for the next 10 years or so (i.e. we included an EV charger load). The advice from Finn was to get as many panels as you can aford at the start, so we went for what we thought would fit on the part of the roof we earmarked for solar, turns out that the Nearmaps tool for placing panels actually showed panel size much larger than reality when compared with the roof size, which means we could have had more panels ... oh well maybe later. 15.9kW of panels is not a bad size for now.Solar Dynamics did not initially want to come out to inform their quote, that was a negative mark against them however we persisted (luckily). Once we had a reasonable panel quantity and arrangment I asked if they could come out, and they were only too happy to visit. Luckily they did because that visit led to enhancements of the system that were not obvious from a desktop quote (I can hear Finn thinking, but not saying out loud, "told you so"), particularly the placement of panels and the selection of the battery. Even so, when the installers arrived they changed the configuration a little to an optimal one based on their experience. Today we are seeing more than 13kW generated at times, 18kWh to the grid (pity the power company is not logging our inputs yet, up to 10 days before that happens, but at least others are using that solar power instead of coal generated power), and the battery was full within a two hours. United is planning an outage for a large part of tomorrow, we have the system running as of today so we will be totally unaffected by the outage.The installers were terrific, very knowledgable, fast, great quality work and helpful (yes, I was there peppering them with questions).

Solar Dynamics quoted on a Tesla Powerwall 2 battery to compliment my 5kw solar system.  The whole process was easy.  The installer was a lovely bloke and very good at his job. I haven’t used power from the grid for over a week. I had been researching solar options for some time when I connected with Solar Dynamics via the SolarQuotes process. They were one of approximately 8 solar companies here in Melbourne that I vetted as part of my wanting to understand everything around my solar options. Of the 8 companies, 2 or 3 were rather basic and underwhelming (dealing mainly with sales folks who wanted to transact quickly rather than educate, and often showing little technical knowledge). 2 or 3 were solid but unspectacular, while 3 or 4 were genuinely outstanding during the research phase.What made them outstanding? They quickly identified that I had a thirst to understand and probe at everything, and they progressed my query to their most senior advisers (usually their owners), who spent hours discussing my options and choices without ever making me feel that I was a difficulty sale - I just wanted to do it well, once. And they provided detailed, considered quotes that provided great insights behind their recommendationsWhy did I settle on Solar Dynamics?They immediately transferred me to the owner, Wayne, who spent a huge amount of time educating and adjusting possible options for my roof - panel brands and types (including 60 cell vs 72 cell panels), straight string inverter or Tigo optimisers on part shaded panels or Solar Edge optimisers on all panels or Enphase microinverters on all panels, battery options for the future etc. Each time I called back to tweak or challenge I felt welcome - Wayne liked that I wanted to know more, despite being a difficult  and uncommitted potential sale. And each time we challenged and tweaked together, we improved the ROI without compromising on the quality of the overall design.Once we finally settled on the proposed structure, I asked for final proposals from the 4 impressive solar companies that I had been talking too. Solar Dynamics proposal was exactly where it needed to be, just slightly lower than two of the others without being silly cheap if that makes sense, and well below the fourth. That, combined with the fact that I found Wayne to be the equal most impressive owner in terms of his knowledge and approach, made the choice simple.My thinking throughout was, in terms of importance: 1) get a great solar company/installer, 2) get a great inverter/microinverter/optimers, 3) get good panels.In Wayne and Solar Dynamics, I felt very comfortable I was getting a great Company/installer - he has a long and established track record in the industry, he has been running just the two installer crews for a number of years, and he is invested in his clients and the goodwill they can create.We chose Enphase for the inversion system, as we were maximising my roof space and therefore had to deal with some minor shade issues - plus I figure while there is a small premium to an Enphase system, it's a 30 year asset, and the ability to have panel by panel immediate feedback on an app will be invaluable in terms of monitoring its performance throughout that time - indeed, that live feedback app immediately identified some small tweaks we needed to do post installation to optimise the system - things we would not have easily found without panel by panel information as we were still producing well, just not fully optimised.Then finally, we settled on Longi 72 cell 450 watt panels, 12 year product warranty, 30 year performance warranty (we have a flat clip-lock roof with a jig-puzzle shape that supported 72 cell panels really well as we could fit 42 of them versus 48 of the 60 cell panels).  Research and a number of the better solar company owners all indicated that these Longi panels were a fairly compelling option. Not quite the BWM panels of Sunpower or LG,  more like a KIA (to paraphrase Finn), but allied with the Enphase monitoring, a strong quality combination - or at least so we hope, 30 years will tell!Installation was done on time and well, with the crew (Stew and Michael) more than happy to indulge my continuing interest throughout their two and half days on my roof.The girls in Solar Dynamics' office then mastered the paperwork in record time, notwithstanding it was almost Christmas, such that the inspector and the connection to the grid was completed in just a couple of days post installation, meaning we were fully live within a week of the installation being completed.I have now referred several friends to Solar Dynamics and Wayne (and am continuing to probe Wayne about their options on their behalf!) I think that reflects how well I think his team has done.I called the Enphase team to ask a question a week or two ago. Their team noted that they had never seen one of their systems so well optimised and performing so strongly. That's high praise of Wayne and his team.It's early days, so obviously reviews like this can be made to look silly if things change.But right now, I fully and unreservedly recommend Wayne and his team.

The price paid of $4,390 is after Victorian rebate and loan, and cashing in STCs. The system is 7.04kW of Sunpower P19 panels with a 6kW Fronius inverter. We also paid the $300ish for the Fronius monitoring module (which I feel was well worth it as I can monitor our electrical demand in near-real time).Wayne from Solar Dynamics visited my house to have a look prior to quoting. He listened very closely to what it was I was trying to achieve with a solar power system and delivered on that. He was also very responsive in making some changes to the quoted system once I had learned more and spoken with other suppliers. In all, a very positive customer experience to this point.The office staff were very helpful during the very trying time when Solar Victoriaâ€™s web portal went to hell in a hand basket, and Iâ€™m certain they (Solar Dynamics staff) were up to their necks in annoyed customers. They handled that situation very well and I was able to secure a rebate slot.The installation was booked, but then moved at their request to accommodate other installations. I was called in advance and politely asked if this was ok, to which I said it wasnâ€™t a problem as the installation was only moved a few days. The installers were polite, accommodating, and turned up more or less on time. The installation was completed by the end of the same day and everything was up and running.At ground level, the installers appeared to have tidied up nicely with a few small items left here and there (I mean really small - easy to miss, so entirely excusable).However, the situation was a little different up on the roof. My system is not a small one, so I wonder if they were rushing to finish that day. There are quite a number of depressions in my corrugated roof where the installers were not standing on the line of battens, though I understand this would certainly be unavoidable some of the time, so itâ€™s just an observation. Of greater concern is the screws that were removed from the roof sheets (presumably to affix the panel racks) and not replaced leaving a hole and water ingress point. I found five screws missing; three in a line on one sheet at the end of the panel array, one on the ridge cap and one in a random other location. Several other screws were not sufficiently threaded in to engage the rubber gasket and seal the hole. I found a few of the original roofing screws in gutters so put them back in the holes myself, and checked all the other screws I could see to make sure my roof is water tight.Substantial scraps across the roof sheets are evident, which will expose the sheets to corrosion. The odd nick here and there is alright, but where something has clearly been dragged across the roof and removed about an A4 sized amount paint is pretty careless and probably should have rectified somehow (even with silicone or a lick of paint). Iâ€™m not worried about aesthetics as my roof is not visible from anywhere on my block, but I am concerned about corrosion.A slightly lesser, but still noteworthy, concern is the amount of swarf left on the roof from drilling new holes. Some of it was big enough to pick up as a sizeable clump, so the amount was not insubstantial. The problem with leaving swarf on a roof is that it rusts as it is not coated like the rest of the roof sheets, which in turn can rust the sheets over time. When I built my garage, I was very conscious of leaving swarf on the roof and swept the whole thing at the end of drilling. I would have expected similar from a professional installer as itâ€™s a quick job at the time but cannot be done now as the panels are installed and in the way.In all, the missing screws were nothing more than an inconvenience that I needed to address as I was on the roof anyway to clean gutters. The problem would be for a person who either isnâ€™t as handy or not able to get on their roof to identify the issue.That aside, the installation of the inverter and all the connections appear solid and professional. The inverter was connected to my WiFi network by the installers before they left, which I appreciated. I donâ€™t have any concerns with the actual installation of the racking, panels or inverter; just the state in which my roof was left.The system has been generating good power and Iâ€™m like a kid with a new toy constantly looking at the Fronius app (which isnâ€™t brilliant as far as apps go, buts thatâ€™s a Fronius thing) to check the output.I would recommend any of the providers that quoted my system, and I would recommend Solar Dynamics as I am very happy with the system that was designed and the price we paid - I feel we achieved very good value-for-money. I would only hope that the installers pay a little more attention during and at the end of the job.
